import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_17_0: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_17_1: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_17_2: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_17_0 and Source3_17_1 on movie_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by Source3_17_1.title, aggregations:
# avg(Source3_17_0.rating) filtered by gender='F' as F,
# avg(Source3_17_0.rating) filtered by gender='M' as M
# But gender is not in join_0_1 yet, so this aggregation cannot be done now.
# According to operation history, this aggregation is done after the first join,
# but gender is only available after joining with Source3_17_2.
# So we will do the aggregation after the next join.

# Operation 3: JOIN Source3_17_0 and Source3_17_2 on user_id
# We need to join df0 and df2 on user_id to get gender info for ratings.
join_0_2 = pd.merge(df0, df2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Operation 4: group_by Source3_17_1.title, aggregations:
# avg(Source3_17_0.rating) filtered by gender='F' as F,
# avg(Source3_17_0.rating) filtered by gender='M' as M
# This means we need to join the rating+gender info with title info (Source3_17_1)
# So join join_0_2 (which has rating and gender) with df1 (which has title) on movie_id
join_all = pd.merge(join_0_2, df1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Now perform the aggregation grouped by title:
# avg rating for gender='F' as F
# avg rating for gender='M' as M

# Filtered averages can be done using conditional aggregation with pandas:
agg_df = join_all.groupby("title").apply(
    lambda g: pd.Series({
        "F": g.loc[g["gender"] == "F", "rating"].mean(),
        "M": g.loc[g["gender"] == "M", "rating"].mean()
    })
).reset_index()

# Ensure columns are in the order and types as per target schema:
# ['title': string, 'F': float, 'M': float]
agg_df = agg_df[["title", "F", "M"]]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/target_multisource.csv"
agg_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_17_0 and Source3_17_2 on user_id
joined_0_2 = pd.merge(source0, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_17_1 on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(joined_0_2, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Compute average rating grouped by title and gender
# Pivot the gender to columns F and M with average ratings
grouped = joined_all.groupby(["title", "gender"], as_index=False)["rating"].mean()

# Pivot gender to columns F and M
pivoted = grouped.pivot(index="title", columns="gender", values="rating").reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
pivoted.columns.name = None
pivoted = pivoted.rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M", "title": "title"})

# The target schema is ['title': string, 'F': float, 'M': float]
# Ensure columns are in the correct order
pivoted = pivoted[["title", "F", "M"]]

# Write to the target file
pivoted.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
